nodes.description: In 2004, Santtu Parikka founded Fake Production, a VR and gaming studio that won multiple awards for animation. In recent years, as our passion for all things VR/AR has grown, we’ve been drawn to an important challenge: to enable people thousands of miles apart to collaborate effectively in virtual environments, just as they might in a real physical setting. In 2016, Santtu and our CXO Juha Ruistola revealed the first multi-user VR prototypes. These proved an instant hit. A year later, as we crystallized our new mission, vision and strategy, Glue was born. Since then, our 30-strong team has continued to build on our legacy and break new ground in multi-user VR software, developing Glue into the fully-featured virtual collaboration platform we are today. Originally created by Markus "Notch" Persson using the Java programming language, until Persson left Mojang and gave Jens "Jeb" Bergensten control over the game's development. In 2014, Mojang and the Minecraft intellectual property were purchased by Microsoft for US$2.5 billion. Minecraft has since become the best-selling video game of all-time, with over 300 million copies sold and nearly 140 million monthly active players as of 2023.

Poptropica is primarily the creation of Jeff Kinney. The game primarily focuses on problem-solving through game quest scenarios, called "islands". Islands all center on a problem that the player must resolve by going through multiple obstacles, collecting and using items, talking to various characters, and completing goals. All islands, upon completion, award "credits," which are non-negotiable currency that may be used to buy costumes and special effects in the Poptropica store.

While Rise is sometimes referred to as a game, in general it does not have points, scores, winners or losers, levels, an end-strategy, or most of the other characteristics of a typical game. Players, often called "citizens", can visit this virtual world almost as if it were a real place. They explore, meet other citizens, socialize, participate in individual and alliance activities, and buy and produce goods (virtual property) and services from one another.

nodes.description: The Sims Online was a 2002 massively multiplayer online game (MMO) developed by Maxis and published by Electronic Arts (EA) for Microsoft Windows. The game was a subscription-based online multiplayer version of the 2000 Maxis game The Sims, in which players could interact with others on virtual user-made lots, buy and customise properties, and make in-game money by taking on jobs. The Sims Online was the project of Maxis founder and Sims creator Will Wright, who sought to create an open-ended online game based on social interaction, with ambitions for the game to be a platform for emergent gameplay and the creation of virtual societies and politics.

nodes.name: Spore
nodes.description: A massively single-player game allowing a player to control the evolution of a species from its beginnings through its development to interstellar exploration. Players can also create vehicles, buildings and spaceships with Creator tools.

nodes.name: Star Atlas
nodes.description: Star Atlas is a space exploration themed role-playing game (RPG) built on the Solana network. The game takes place in the year 2620, with political factions, territorial pursuit, high-tech weaponry and space craft enriching different aspects of the gameplay.

nodes.name: Stardoll
nodes.description: A virtual world designed for girls ages 7 to 17 where they can design clothes for their own avatar doll or for celebrity dolls and meet friends from all over the globe.

nodes.name: TamaTown
nodes.description: A virtual world with entire families of avatar characters which can be selected based on personality characteristics, the there are games, gifts, friends and there’s a new addition called Tama & Earth Expo for travel to virtual pavilions that showcase real world locations and visit the ecology pavilion to learn how to help save the planet.

nodes.name: Tower Unite
nodes.description: Tower Unite is a 2016 virtual world party game and sandbox game developed by PixelTail Games, in active development and available as an early access title on Steam. The game is set on an island in the style of a resort theme park, where players can interact, play mini-games, and join lobbies via matchmaking. In addition, players can host public or private virtual spaces known as "condos", customized with furniture and props.

nodes.name: Transformice
nodes.description: Transformice is an online multiplayer free-to-play platform and indie game by Atelier 801. Created by French game designers, Melibellule produces the game's artwork and graphics, while Tigrounette programs the game's functions and mechanics. Transformice was released as a browser game in 2010, and on Steam as a free-to-play game on in 2015. The main objective of the game is to collect a piece of cheese placed in at least one location on a map. As of 2012, the game has 10 million accounts created, 60 million as of 2015, 70 million as of 2017, and 100 million as of 2019.

nodes.name: Treetures
nodes.description: A virtual world for kids with forest theme where kids get to plant trees and care for them.

nodes.name: Underlight
nodes.description: https://wiki.underlight.com/Main_Page MMORPG released originally in 1998 on Mplayer. Game takes place inside a "Dream" that gifted people can access when they sleep. Roleplaying strictly enforced and OOC chatting about real world stuff is not allowed.

nodes.name: Urbaniacs
nodes.description: A virtual world where members can create their own characters, play games and do battle, interact with friends and shop.

nodes.name: Virtual Congress
nodes.description:
From the University of Indiana a virtual world designed to let high school students experience the workings of the real Congress through MMORPG activities like committee hearings, writing amendments and meeting with virtual constituents.

Playing is via Discord

nodes.name: vTime XR*
nodes.description: vTime XR is a free-to-play virtual reality and augmented reality social network created by British virtual and augmented reality innovation company vTime Limited, developed in Liverpool in the UK.

nodes.name: Webkinz
nodes.description: Webkinz is a stuffed animal and video game franchise by the Canadian toy company Ganz. Webkinz stuffed animals have online counterparts in the video games Webkinz Classic and Webkinz Next. It was originally released by Ganz on April 15, 2005. Each Webkinz toy has an attached tag with a unique "secret code" printed on it, allowing its owner to play with a digital version of their pet on iOS, Android, and desktop computers.

nodes.name: Whyville
nodes.description: Launched in 1999, Whyville is an educational Internet site geared towards children aged 8–14, founded and managed by Numedeon Inc. Whyville engages its uses in learning about a broad range of topics, including science, business, art and geography.

nodes.name: Wizard101
nodes.description: Online game and 3D virtual world with quests, seven schools of magic, pets to adopt, puzzles and minigames, and accessories available for purchase.

nodes.name: Woozworld
nodes.description: Woozworld is a virtual gaming community and social network service founded in 2009 and headquartered in Montreal, Quebec. Woozworld allows users to connect with each other through customizable profiles and interactive activities. Woozworld is a virtual gaming community and social network for kids that allows users to create their own online realities, interact with others, and express themselves.

nodes.name: World of Neopia
nodes.description: An updated Neopets with new links and new activities.

nodes.name: Worldwide Webb
nodes.description: Worldwide Webb is an interoperable pixel art MMORPG metaverse game giving utility to popular NFT projects. The game uses NFTs for in-game avatars, pets, lands, NFT Items , and quests.

nodes.name: Yohoho! Puzzle Pirates
nodes.description: A virtual world based on the pirate theme and filled with games and puzzles. Players can explore and interact with their avatar, accept challenges, own property and buy, sell and trade virtual goods.

nodes.name: Zenith
nodes.description: Launched in 2022, Zenith: The Last City is a virtual reality open world massively multiplayer online role-playing game (MMORPG) developed and published by Californian game development studio Ramen VR.

nodes.name: Decentraland
nodes.description: Decentraland is a browser‑based, Ethereum‑powered 3D virtual realm where users truly own their creations—from parcels of digital land to wearable NFTs—and shape the world through community governance. In this decentralized metaverse, you can buy, build, and monetize unique experiences, from art galleries and concert venues to mini‑games and virtual storefronts, using the native MANA token and LAND and Estate NFTs. Powered by a DAO, users vote on platform decisions and proposals, ensuring the ecosystem evolves by and for the community.

nodes.name: dverso
nodes.description: Dverso is a free, browser-based, blockchain-ready 3D metaverse platform that empowers users to explore and build immersive virtual environments collaboratively in real time. With its intuitive editor, physics engine, and visual scripting tools, creators can launch mini‑worlds—from games and social hubs to NFT‑enabled experiences—without needing third‑party software. Founder‑led and launched in open alpha from Milan, it supports NFT integration, live streaming, avatars, and in‑world economies, making it a versatile sandbox for education, entertainment, community, and commerce. More than 900 user‑created maps have already been realized, showcasing Dverso's flexibility for crafting rich, interactive web‑metaverse experiences.

nodes.name: High Street
nodes.description: Highstreet is a pioneering commerce‑centric metaverse that combines immersive gaming, virtual reality, and blockchain-powered shopping. In this VR/MMO world—accessible via browser or headsets like Oculus Quest—players explore, complete quests, and engage in action combat, all while earning in‑game rewards and discovering “phygital” items: digital assets that can be redeemed for real‑world products. Powered by its native HIGH and STREET tokens, Highstreet integrates NFT collectible mechanics with dynamic pricing curves, ensuring liquidity and authenticity across its marketplace . Supported by major backers like Binance Labs and Animoca Brands, and evolving through staged VR content (from themed campus demos to an upcoming Gladiator Arena), Highstreet offers a vivid, playful fusion of retail, adventure, and social metaverse interaction.

nodes.name: Hyperfy
nodes.description: Hyperfy is a dynamic, browser-based metaverse platform that empowers creators to design, own, and trade fully immersive virtual worlds as NFTs built on Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, and Optimism. Without requiring coding or extensive 3D design skills, users can assemble interactive experiences—galleries, games, venues, shops, and more—using a React‑based builder framework with drag‑and‑drop apps, Web3 hooks, token‑gating, and rich multimedia support. One of its standout features is seamless avatar interoperability via the open VRM standard, allowing users to import and instantly switch VRM avatars in multiplayer sessions across desktop, mobile, or VR. With a fixed supply of 10,000 world NFTs available for minting and trading on platforms like OpenSea, every world is unique, portable, and built for easy collaboration, offering a richly customizable gateway into the open metaverse.

nodes.name: hytopia
nodes.description: Hytopia is a Minecraft‑inspired, blockchain‑powered open‑world platform engineered from the ground up in Rust to offer high‑performance, cross‑platform gameplay on PC, browser, consoles, and mobile. Born from the original “NFT Worlds” Minecraft modding community, the project pivoted after Minecraft prohibited blockchain integration, rebranding and building its own ecosystem with proprietary Hychain Layer 2 technology and a native $TOPIA token used for network fees, staking, governance, and in‑game transactions. Hytopia empowers creators with flexible APIs, self‑serve tools, and NFT‑based “Worlds,” avatars, and items—enabling the launch, monetization, and trading of user‑generated content in a decentralized, community‑driven metaverse. After raising over $8M through node and seed rounds and hitting more than a million pre‑registrations, the platform has already begun alpha and closed beta tests featuring friend lists, community games, chat tools, and ongoing marketplace integration.

nodes.name: Mona
nodes.description: Monaverse (aka MONA) is a blockchain‑powered, open metaverse platform that empowers creators to design, share, collect, and monetize immersive 3D worlds—all accessible via web browser without needing to buy virtual land. Built around interoperable game assets and SDK tools for Unity and Blender, it supports token-gated spaces, voice/text chat, live events, and NFT minting of full interactive environments. Backed by major investors like Protocol Labs, Mona has attracted thousands of builders, artists, and institutions (including Tom Sachs and Moonbirds) to craft photorealistic architecture, dynamic gardens, exhibitions, concerts, and community experiences within “spaces” minted directly as NFTs.

nodes.name: Oncyber
nodes.description: Oncyber is a browser‑based, blockchain‑powered metaverse platform that empowers artists and collectors to build fully immersive 3D/VR spaces to showcase their digital assets and NFTs. It supports multi‑chain integration (Ethereum, Solana, Polygon, and more), enabling seamless display and provenance of NFTs within customizable galleries and environments. Behind the scenes, Oncyber employs high-performance GPU‑based graphics and advanced optimizations—such as avatar instancing, texture atlasing, and LOD—to deliver hundreds of animated avatars running at up to 120 FPS, even in large shared virtual events. With its intuitive Studio editor and evolving AI tools like Magic Composer, users—regardless of technical skill—can create dynamic, responsive virtual worlds with real-time lighting, architecture, scripting, and more, all accessible instantly via browser.

nodes.name: Ozone Metaverse
nodes.description: Ozone Metaverse is a pioneering Web3 cloud platform that enables anyone—from individuals and creators to brands and governments—to build, explore, and monetize immersive 3D environments directly in a browser. Powered by its proprietary O3 graphics engine and scalable cloud infrastructure, it offers seamless integration across desktop, mobile, VR, and AR. With a versatile toolkit (no-code studio, AI-driven NPCs, NFT asset pipelines, live services) and interoperable Web3 support, users can collaborate on dynamic virtual worlds, hold in-world commerce, and participate in decentralized governance—all without writing a single line of code.

nodes.name: Portal
nodes.description: Portals is a browser-based, no-code metaverse built on the Solana blockchain that invites users to create, explore, and socialize in fully customizable 3D worlds—no downloads or VR gear required. Often described as the "Roblox of web3," the platform enables users to mint virtual land as Solana NFTs, then design immersive rooms, games, and galleries within an interactive digital city. Seamless wallet integration (via Phantom, Solflare, etc.), fast on-chain transactions, and built-in social features like voice chat make Portals accessible and community-driven. Its focus on user-generated content and low-friction entry point aims to democratize the metaverse and empower creativity across the Solana ecosystem.

nodes.name: Red Fox
nodes.description: RFOX is a VR‑first, Web3 metaverse offering AI‑enabled creator tools and white‑label solutions for immersive experiences. The platform includes RFOX VALT, a fully interactive virtual space for retail, entertainment, and social interaction. Powered by bespoke APIs and SDKs, RFOX empowers creators and brands to launch experiences without heavy technical overhead.

nodes.name: Sandbox
nodes.description: The Sandbox is a decentralized virtual world built on the Ethereum blockchain that allows users to create, own, and monetize interactive experiences using NFTs and the native SAND token. Through tools like VoxEdit and Game Maker, users can design assets and games without coding, placing them on virtual land parcels known as LAND. The platform emphasizes user-generated content, digital ownership, and economic participation, with major brands like Gucci, Atari, and Warner Music establishing a presence within its immersive ecosystem.

nodes.name: Somnium Space
nodes.description: Somnium Space is an open, VR‑centric metaverse built on Ethereum, accessible via PC, mobile, and major VR headsets. It offers persistent worlds where users can buy land, create avatars, build and monetize VR experiences, and earn through content and event hosting. Its native token, CUBE, underpins the in‑world economy.

nodes.name: Substrata (XR Showcase)
nodes.description: Substrata is an open‑source, browser‑based 3D metaverse emphasizing vast, persistent worlds with minimal technical limits. Free to explore and build within, users benefit from long render distances and the ability to host on custom servers. Originally conceived to rival the traditional “2D web,” Substrata prioritizes decentralization and creative freedom.

nodes.name: The Nemesis
nodes.description: The Nemesis is a multi‑device virtual world blending Web2/3, VR/AR, and play‑to‑earn gaming. Users can explore branded virtual environments, use 25+ vehicle types (cars, aircraft, horses), and earn via mobile or web access. Its Creator Studio supports user‑generated content, with native NEMS tokens and AR‑enhanced interactivity.

nodes.name: Upland
nodes.description: Upland is a property trading metaverse mapped to real-world cities, built on EOS. Users can buy, sell, and develop virtual real estate, engaging in play‑to‑earn mechanics through land flipping and treasure‑hunting. It operates like a blockchain “Monopoly,” attracting both gamers and virtual real estate investors.

nodes.name: Utherverse
nodes.description: Utherverse is an interconnected network of social 3D worlds powered by photorealistic avatars built in Unity. Available across multiple devices (PC, mobile, VR), it emphasizes real-time social interaction, events, virtual business (e.g. property and event management), and even adult‑oriented spaces.

nodes.name: VictoriaVR
nodes.description: Victoria VR is a blockchain‑driven, AI‑powered VR MMORPG developed in Unreal Engine 5. It features hyper-realistic graphics, user‑created worlds via an AI builder, DAO governance, tokenized land, and a rewards model that returns 50% of asset sale revenue to users. The native VR token fuels its social, gaming, and economic systems.

nodes.name: Voxels (formerly Cryptovoxels)
nodes.description: Voxels is a browser‑based, Ethereum NFT metaverse where users build, own, and trade voxel art, wearables, land, and experiences. Celebrated for its grassroots creator economy and decentralized governance, it fosters collaborative world‑building and artistic expression.

nodes.name: Wilder World
nodes.description: Wilder World is a photorealistic, blockchain-powered open-world metaverse built on Unreal Engine, where users—known as Wilders—can explore, race, fight, and build within a sprawling city called Wiami. Every in-game asset—from avatars and vehicles to land and fashion—is tokenized as NFTs with real utility, tradeable on the Wilder World Metaverse Market and secured by the native $WILD token.

nodes.name: Poptropica
nodes.description: Poptropica is an online role-playing game, developed in 2007 by Pearson Education's Family Education Network, and targeted towards children aged 6 to 15. Poptropica is primarily the creation of Jeff Kinney. The game primarily focuses on problem-solving through game quest scenarios, called "islands". Islands all center on a problem that the player must resolve by going through multiple obstacles, collecting and using items, talking to various characters, and completing goals. All islands, upon completion, award "credits," which are non-negotiable currency that may be used to buy costumes and special effects in the Poptropica store.

nodes.name: Rise: The Vieneo Province
nodes.description: Rise: The Vieneo Province (abbreviated to Rise) is an MMO space simulator. The game is centered around an exomoon called Vieneo about 225 LY from Earth. While Rise is sometimes referred to as a game, in general it does not have points, scores, winners or losers, levels, an end-strategy, or most of the other characteristics of a typical game. Players, often called "citizens", can visit this virtual world almost as if it were a real place. They explore, meet other citizens, socialize, participate in individual and alliance activities, and buy and produce goods (virtual property) and services from one another.

nodes.name: SIMS Online
nodes.description: The Sims Online was a 2002 massively multiplayer online game (MMO) developed by Maxis and published by Electronic Arts (EA) for Microsoft Windows. The game was a subscription-based online multiplayer version of the 2000 Maxis game The Sims, in which players could interact with others on virtual user-made lots, buy and customise properties, and make in-game money by taking on jobs. The Sims Online was the project of Maxis founder and Sims creator Will Wright, who sought to create an open-ended online game based on social interaction, with ambitions for the game to be a platform for emergent gameplay and the creation of virtual societies and politics.

The game was a subscription-based online multiplayer version of the 2000 Maxis game The Sims, in which players could interact with others on virtual user-made lots, buy and customise properties, and make in-game money by taking on jobs. The Sims Online was the project of Maxis founder and Sims creator Will Wright, who sought to create an open-ended online game based on social interaction, with ambitions for the game to be a platform for emergent gameplay and the creation of virtual societies and politics.

nodes.name: Transformice
nodes.description: Transformice is an online multiplayer free-to-play platform and indie game by Atelier 801. Created by French game designers, Melibellule produces the game's artwork and graphics, while Tigrounette programs the game's functions and mechanics. Transformice was released as a browser game in 2010, and on Steam as a free-to-play game on in 2015. The main objective of the game is to collect a piece of cheese placed in at least one location on a map. As of 2012, the game has 10 million accounts created, 60 million as of 2015, 70 million as of 2017, and 100 million as of 2019.

nodes.name: dverso
nodes.description: Dverso is a free, browser-based, blockchain-ready 3D metaverse platform that empowers users to explore and build immersive virtual environments collaboratively in real time. With its intuitive editor, physics engine, and visual scripting tools, creators can launch mini‑worlds—from games and social hubs to NFT‑enabled experiences—without needing third‑party software. More than 900 user‑created maps have already been realized, showcasing Dverso's flexibility for crafting rich, interactive web‑metaverse experiences.

nodes.name: High Street
nodes.description: Highstreet is a pioneering commerce‑centric metaverse that combines immersive gaming, virtual reality, and blockchain-powered shopping. In this VR/MMO world—accessible via browser or headsets like Oculus Quest—players explore, complete quests, and engage in action combat, all while earning in‑game rewards and discovering “phygital” items: digital assets that can be redeemed for real‑world products. Powered by its native HIGH and STREET tokens, Highstreet integrates NFT collectible mechanics with dynamic pricing curves, ensuring liquidity and authenticity across its marketplace . Supported by major backers like Binance Labs and Animoca Brands, and evolving through staged VR content (from themed campus demos to an upcoming Gladiator Arena), Highstreet offers a vivid, playful fusion of retail, adventure, and social metaverse interaction.

nodes.name: Hyperfy
nodes.description: Hyperfy is a dynamic, browser-based metaverse platform that empowers creators to design, own, and trade fully immersive virtual worlds as NFTs built on Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, and Optimism. Without requiring coding or extensive 3D design skills, users can assemble interactive experiences—galleries, games, venues, shops, and more—using a React‑based builder framework with drag‑and‑drop apps, Web3 hooks, token‑gating, and rich multimedia support. One of its standout features is seamless avatar interoperability via the open VRM standard, allowing users to import and instantly switch VRM avatars in multiplayer sessions across desktop, mobile, or VR. With a fixed supply of 10,000 world NFTs available for minting and trading on platforms like OpenSea, every world is unique, portable, and built for easy collaboration, offering a richly customizable gateway into the open metaverse.

nodes.name: hytopia
nodes.description: Hytopia is a Minecraft‑inspired, blockchain‑powered open‑world platform engineered from the ground up in Rust to offer high‑performance, cross‑platform gameplay on PC, browser, consoles, and mobile. Born from the original “NFT Worlds” Minecraft modding community, the project pivoted after Minecraft prohibited blockchain integration, rebranding and building its own ecosystem with proprietary Hychain Layer 2 technology and a native $TOPIA token used for network fees, staking, governance, and in‑game transactions. Hytopia empowers creators with flexible APIs, self‑serve tools, and NFT‑based “Worlds,” avatars, and items—enabling the launch, monetization, and trading of user‑generated content in a decentralized, community‑driven metaverse. After raising over $8M through node and seed rounds and hitting more than a million pre‑registrations, the platform has already begun alpha and closed beta tests featuring friend lists, community games, chat tools, and ongoing marketplace integration.

nodes.name: Mona
nodes.description: Monaverse (aka MONA) is a blockchain‑powered, open metaverse platform that empowers creators to design, share, collect, and monetize immersive 3D worlds—all accessible via web browser without needing to buy virtual land. Built around interoperable game assets and SDK tools for Unity and Blender, it supports token-gated spaces, voice/text chat, live events, and NFT minting of full interactive environments. Backed by major investors like Protocol Labs, Mona has attracted thousands of builders, artists, and institutions (including Tom Sachs and Moonbirds) to craft photorealistic architecture, dynamic gardens, exhibitions, concerts, and community experiences within “spaces” minted directly as NFTs.
